terms.grammar: future imperative of habeō, with tēcum
evidence: Cic. Att. 4.15.6: vērum haec tū tēcum habētō (Lewis & Short), s.v. habeō
Cic. Fam. 7.25.2: sēcrētō hoc audī, tēcum habētō, nē Apellae quidem lībertō tuō dīxeris (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Cicero’s way of sharing a secret in a letter. The future imperative habētō is the form of standing instructions.

phrases.latin: sēcrētō hoc audī, tēcum habētō, nē Apellae quidem lībertō tuō dīxeris
phrases.english: hear this in confidence and keep it to yourself; don’t tell even your freedman Apella

sources: Lewis & Short: habeo
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 101, checked against the searchable text and the page image (12 November 2026).
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
